summary: Built by the CCC in 1939 as a rustic sandstone lookout in Mesa Verde; restored in 2009, it is still used in fire season, with no current staffing schedule found.

facts.design: Native sandstone, 17 ft octagonal floor plan, rustic National Park Service design quarried and worked on Chapin Mesa (1939, Civilian Conservation Corps)
facts.agency: National Park Service, Mesa Verde National Park

staffing.status: Used by the park during fire season (NPS page); a 2009 account said it would be staffed through the summer; the 2009 register visit found it unstaffed that day

access.note: Overlook parking and trailhead are open; the road is not plowed in winter, so access is limited then; the lookout was open to the public during staffed summer months per the 2009 account

visit.trail_note: Parking, a trailhead, a seasonal restroom and a vault toilet at the overlook; the road up is not plowed in winter

events.note: Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps with a rustic design; completion in August 1939 per the December 1939 Mesa Verde Notes
Lookout observer posted from completion; sleeping and cooking facilities were provided inside so the observer was always on hand
Restoration using park funds; dedication held June 10, 2009, the same occasion that recognized the NHLR listing
Registered May 1, 2009 as NHLR US 806, CO 10
NHLR condition note: cab in good condition; walkway around the lookout could use painting and repair; interior floors and electronics could use work

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 8,571 ft (2,612 m) and the National Park Service gives 8,572 feet (2,612 m). Both match the record's 2612.4 m to the nearest meter, so the record was kept.

The 2009 register visit found it unstaffed, with rangers saying it might stay unstaffed that season. The 2009 success story said it would be staffed through the summer. The current NPS page says it is used during fire season and gives no staffing schedule. Treated as seasonal; not confirmed for 2026.

notes_for_editor: The brief's kind 'ground' may be wrong. The NHLR visit form asks about stairs and a walkway around the 'LO', which suggests an elevated cab, but no source states the height or structure type, so the record was not changed. Dates rest on NHLR (1939, 2009), the 2009 NFP success story, and the December 1939 Mesa Verde Notes. No current staffing schedule was found; the NHLR visit reports are from 2009 and 2019. The 2009 success story names the fire management officer differently in the caption and body, so no name is used. The Wikidata and OpenStreetMap pages in the brief were not read. The parkcation.com trail page was seen in search results but not read.
